correctness.rationale: For any permutation carrying each element into its principal ideal, inclusions along a permutation cycle force ideal equality. Apply this separately to theta(x)=x alpha(x) and delta=theta composed with alpha^{-1}; at x and alpha(x) this gives (x)=(x alpha(x))=(alpha(x))=(x^2). Thus x=x^2 b for some b and no nonzero nilpotent can exist. The finite commutative Artinian decomposition is therefore into fields. Principal ideals distinguish supports, so alpha and theta permute each individual one-coordinate nonzero stratum, even if alpha was not assumed coordinatewise. In an odd field the product over this stratum yields -1=1, and in F_2 the lone nonzero point and zero both map to zero under x+alpha(x). Conversely scalar multiplication by a not in {0,1} gives invertible alpha and x+alpha(x), and x alpha(x)=a x^2 is invertible by Frobenius. Both separate witnesses on F_2 x F_4 work, the additive witness after an F_2-linear identification with F_8. The excluded zero ring would be a separate trivial case.
residual_risks: Existence classification only, not an enumeration of all admissible maps or an extension to noncommutative rings. The proof is not formal verification.

evidence: Theorem 2.1 gives a regularity obstruction in the finite semigroup setting; Theorem 3.3 treats preservation of Green-class structure. Neither imposes a second operation.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general theory supplies the multiplicative structural reduction, but one-operation existence does not imply one shared permutation; in particular it does not exclude an F_2 factor. The new classification is not credited for the semigroup regularity step.

evidence: Multiplicative regularity allows F_2; the additive group of F_2 x F_4 admits a complete map although support preservation forces any multiplicatively complete permutation to fix the F_2 idempotent.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither the multiplicative semigroup theorem nor separate additive existence settles simultaneous existence. The support-by-support obstruction using both operations and the sufficiency construction resolve that gap rather than just evaluating parameters in a prior classification.

evidence: Problem 15.12 explicitly gives the simultaneous-operation formulation including addition and multiplication of a finite ring.
Zieve's complete permutation polynomial condition is bijectivity of f and x+f(x), without the product map.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A common choice of rows and columns for both transversals gives exactly the three permutations in the finding. The prior problem asks for criteria, whereas the polynomial convention alone is strictly weaker than the simultaneous predicate.

evidence: The cubic-residue result counts permutation and complete-polynomial fiber maps for q congruent to 1 mod 9, not simultaneous multiplication and addition.
The linear strata result counts B with B, A_1+B and A_2+B invertible in dimension two, not a ring-product transversal.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: Neither closest catalogue statement or count supplies the classified predicate over arbitrary finite commutative unital rings.

originality.rationale: Best of current knowledge: the supported distinct claim is the simultaneous existence classification on finite nonzero commutative unital rings, a precise instance of a published question, not regularity or complete mappings for either operation alone.
residual_risks: Bounded comparisons do not rule out an unindexed equivalent under common-transversal terminology. An empty focused literature lookup did not provide evidence of absence.

value.rationale: A complete existence criterion and explicit witnesses answer the finite commutative unital case of the simultaneous-operations question. The two-operation obstruction on F_2 x F_4 shows why this is not just two independent applications of known complete-mapping criteria.
residual_risks: Value is in the full scoped criterion, not in the small-ring computations or a claim to settle the broader semigroup problem.
